transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me today?

Um… yeah. I think, I guess work wanted me to come. It’s not like I’m trying to cause problems or anything. At the warehouse I’ve been, uh… doing stuff that looks weird to people, I guess.

Like sometimes I kind of freeze near the forklift with my arms up, or I copy the beeping sounds and the hand signals. And I’ve moved boxes into these little patterns even when people are telling me to stop. I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to be difficult. That’s just what they said was happening, so… that’s why I’m here.
Have you noticed these kinds of behaviors—like freezing in positions, repeating sounds, or arranging things in patterns—since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently?

I don’t think it was, like, from when I was a kid. Not really. I mean, I was maybe a little odd sometimes, but this stuff at work—the confusing way I talk sometimes, and the things they say are strange behaviors at the warehouse—that’s more recent.

It’s been… maybe about six months? Around there. I hope that makes sense.
Over these past six months, have you noticed your mood being unusually high, irritable, or 'wired,' along with having a lot more energy or needing much less sleep than usual?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like, super happy or wired or anything. I mean, I get tense sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had all this extra energy or that I don’t need sleep.

I’m not sure if I’m answering that right, but… no, I haven’t really noticed that kind of thing.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs that others tell you aren't true, during this time?

Um… I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve had, like, voices talking to me or anything like that. Sometimes things feel… confusing, but I wouldn’t want to say it’s something that isn’t real if I’m not sure.

People have told me I’m wrong about stuff at work, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by beliefs. I’m trying to answer the right way.
Have you had any recent illnesses, head injuries, new medications, or been using any drugs or alcohol around the time these behaviors started?

I don’t think so… not that I can remember. I haven’t had, like, a head injury or anything I’d connect to it. And I’m not really on anything new.

I mean, I might be forgetting something small, but nothing that seems important. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you have any ongoing medical conditions—like thyroid problems, seizures, diabetes, or other neurological or autoimmune issues—that a doctor has diagnosed you with?

Um… not that I know of. I haven’t been told I have thyroid problems or seizures or anything like that.

I mean, I don’t go to the doctor a ton, so I don’t want to say absolutely, but nobody’s diagnosed me with something like that, as far as I know.

You mentioned sometimes talking in a confusing way—can you tell me more about that? For example, do you find your thoughts jumping around, or do others have trouble following what you're trying to say?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t try to be confusing. I think I’m explaining it right at the time.

Like at work, if my supervisor asks which pallets are going on the truck, I’ll start with the load sheet, but then I kind of… jump to something else, like my old house, or fishing, or church boxes, and then I come back around or I think I do. But by then people are just looking at me like they don’t know what I’m saying.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I’m not trying to waste time or anything. My thoughts just kind of move too fast or sideways, maybe. Is that what you mean?

You mentioned people have told you that you're wrong about certain things at work—can you tell me more about what you believe is happening there, and whether you still feel it's true even when others disagree?

I’m not sure I’d call it, like, a belief exactly. It’s more that I’ll be pretty sure I understood something at work, like where something was supposed to go or what someone said, and then people tell me, “No, that’s not right.”

Usually I try to just accept it, because I don’t want to argue or make things harder. Sometimes in the moment I still feel like I was right, but then I second-guess myself after. I don’t know if that answers it right.

During these episodes, have you or others noticed any physical symptoms like fever, sweating, muscle stiffness, tremors, or a racing heartbeat happening along with the freezing or repeating behaviors?

Um… I don’t think there was fever or anything like that. At least nobody told me that.

What people notice more is… the freezing part, I guess. Like at the warehouse I’ll kind of stop with my arms up near the forklift, or I start copying the beeping sounds or the hand signals. Sometimes I move boxes around in these little patterns, and people are yelling for me to stop, but I’m not trying to be weird or make trouble.

I don’t know about sweating or heart racing. I’m usually just focused on what I’m doing, if that makes sense.
During these episodes of freezing or repeating behaviors, do you ever feel confused about where you are or lose track of time, or do you stay fully alert and aware of your surroundings?

I think I’m mostly aware, like I know I’m at the warehouse. I don’t think I’m blacking out or anything.

It’s more like I get stuck on doing the thing… like holding my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeps and hand signals, or arranging the boxes in a pattern. People are yelling for me to stop, and I hear them, I think, but it’s hard to switch off right away. I know that sounds bad. I’m just trying to explain it right.

Outside of these episodes at work, have you noticed any changes in your emotions or social life—like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, pulling away from friends or family, or feeling like your emotions are flatter than before?

I don’t know… I guess I haven’t really paid attention to that.

I mean, I still talk to people when I need to, and I’m not trying to shut anyone out. Maybe I’m a little quieter than before, but that could just be stress or being tired. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

As far as emotions being flatter… I’m not sure what that would feel like exactly. I think I’m mostly normal? Does that make sense?
Is there anything you've come to believe about work—like people being against you, monitoring you, or trying to harm you—that you feel is true even when others insist it isn't?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, work can feel tense sometimes, like people get annoyed with me when I’m doing something wrong, but I don’t really think they’re out to hurt me or anything.

I haven’t noticed anyone monitoring me in some special way. If they’re watching me, it’s probably just because I’m at work and they’re trying to make sure things get done right. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming people there, because I’m not.
Over these past six months, have you noticed any change in your motivation to do everyday things—like keeping up with personal hygiene, hobbies you used to enjoy, or tasks at home?

Um… I’m not really sure. I mean, I still get up and go to work, and I do what I have to do mostly.

At home, maybe I let stuff sit longer than I should, but I don’t know if that’s motivation or just being tired. Hygiene is… I think it’s okay. I shower, maybe not always right when I should, but I’m not trying to be gross or anything.

Hobbies, I don’t really have a lot going on right now. I guess I haven’t been doing much besides work and coming home. But I don’t know if that counts as a change. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Compared to how you were functioning before these episodes started about six months ago—at work, at home, and with relationships—do you feel your overall ability to manage things has gotten noticeably worse?

Yeah… I guess if I’m being honest, it has gotten worse. I don’t like saying that because I feel like it makes me sound irresponsible, but… there have been some problems.

At work they took me off the forklift, so I’m just doing other stuff now. They said it was about safety and people not being able to count on me the same way. And I’ve fallen behind in my community college classes too.

I also stopped showing up for the church food-bank shifts. I didn’t mean to just disappear, but I guess they were saying they couldn’t really rely on me there either. So… yeah, I guess overall I’m not managing things like I was before. Is that what you mean?
During these past six months, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or down on yourself, more days than not?

I don’t think it’s been like that, no… not more days than not. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, especially when I mess things up or people are disappointed, but I wouldn’t say I’m just sad all the time or hopeless.

Maybe I’ve been more stressed than anything. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. If you mean like depressed every day, I don’t think that’s really me.

target_item.reason: The question is directly about the freezing and repeating behaviors during episodes, which matches the disorganized or abnormal behavior profile.

patient.answer:
I think I’m mostly aware, like I know I’m at the warehouse. I don’t think I’m blacking out or anything.

It’s more like I get stuck on doing the thing… like holding my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeps and hand signals, or arranging the boxes in a pattern. People are yelling for me to stop, and I hear them, I think, but it’s hard to switch off right away. I know that sounds bad. I’m just trying to explain it right.

inference.note: Patient continues to endorse catatonic features (posturing, echolalia/echopraxia, stereotypy) with disorganized/tangential speech, but remains oriented and alert throughout episodes, arguing against delirium. No autonomic instability, fever, or medical/substance cause identified, and no clear hallucinations or fixed delusions reported. This keeps catatonia associated with a primary psychotic disorder (F20.2) versus catatonia due to another/unspecified mental disorder (F06.1) as the leading possibilities.

doctor.intent: Assess for negative/psychotic symptoms outside the catatonic episodes (e.g., social withdrawal, flattened affect, odd beliefs) that would support an underlying schizophrenic process rather than a purely medical/organic cause
doctor.question: Outside of these episodes at work, have you noticed any changes in your emotions or social life—like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, pulling away from friends or family, or feeling like your emotions are flatter than before?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about negative symptoms such as reduced interest, social withdrawal, or flat emotions, which are not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I guess I haven’t really paid attention to that.

I mean, I still talk to people when I need to, and I’m not trying to shut anyone out. Maybe I’m a little quieter than before, but that could just be stress or being tired. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

As far as emotions being flatter… I’m not sure what that would feel like exactly. I think I’m mostly normal? Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has any fixed false beliefs (delusions) that persist despite evidence against them, to differentiate psychotic disorder from a catatonia secondary to another medical/psychiatric condition
doctor.question: Is there anything you've come to believe about work—like people being against you, monitoring you, or trying to harm you—that you feel is true even when others insist it isn't?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about paranoid or persecutory beliefs/delusions at work, but the provided symptom profile only covers disorganized speech, abnormal behavior, functional impairment, and duration, not delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, work can feel tense sometimes, like people get annoyed with me when I’m doing something wrong, but I don’t really think they’re out to hurt me or anything.

I haven’t noticed anyone monitoring me in some special way. If they’re watching me, it’s probably just because I’m at work and they’re trying to make sure things get done right. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming people there, because I’m not.

inference.note: No evidence of medical, neurological, or substance-related etiology after thorough review, reducing likelihood of F06.1. Catatonic signs (posturing, echophenomena, stereotypies) combined with disorganized speech and lack of mood or clear psychotic symptoms support a primary psychotic disorder with catatonic features (F20.2) rather than a secondary catatonic syndrome.

doctor.intent: Assess for negative symptoms (avolition, self-care, motivation) that support a schizophrenia diagnosis and functional decline
doctor.question: Over these past six months, have you noticed any change in your motivation to do everyday things—like keeping up with personal hygiene, hobbies you used to enjoy, or tasks at home?

target_item.reason: The question is about motivation/avolition and self-care or home activities, which are not specifically covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Um… I’m not really sure. I mean, I still get up and go to work, and I do what I have to do mostly.

At home, maybe I let stuff sit longer than I should, but I don’t know if that’s motivation or just being tired. Hygiene is… I think it’s okay. I shower, maybe not always right when I should, but I’m not trying to be gross or anything.

Hobbies, I don’t really have a lot going on right now. I guess I haven’t been doing much besides work and coming home. But I don’t know if that counts as a change. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

inference.note: Catatonic features (posturing, echolalia/echopraxia, stereotyped patterning behaviors, waxy resistance to stopping) confirmed without mood episode, substance/medical cause, or clear delusions/hallucinations; disorganized speech (tangentiality) supports underlying psychotic process consistent with catatonic schizophrenia. No new alternative diagnoses supported.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there has been a clear decline in overall functioning (work, self-care, relationships) since symptoms began, which is required to support a schizophrenia diagnosis rather than a brief or mood-related psychotic process.
doctor.question: Compared to how you were functioning before these episodes started about six months ago—at work, at home, and with relationships—do you feel your overall ability to manage things has gotten noticeably worse?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve lost my forklift duties, fallen behind in my community-college classes, and stopped showing up for the church food-bank shifts because people say they can’t count on me or keep things safe around me anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether overall functioning at work, home, and relationships has noticeably worsened compared with before the episodes, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess if I’m being honest, it has gotten worse. I don’t like saying that because I feel like it makes me sound irresponsible, but… there have been some problems.

At work they took me off the forklift, so I’m just doing other stuff now. They said it was about safety and people not being able to count on me the same way. And I’ve fallen behind in my community college classes too.

I also stopped showing up for the church food-bank shifts. I didn’t mean to just disappear, but I guess they were saying they couldn’t really rely on me there either. So… yeah, I guess overall I’m not managing things like I was before. Is that what you mean?

inference.note: Continued endorsement of catatonic features (posturing, echolalia/echopraxia, stereotyped behaviors), disorganized speech, and functional decline over 6 months without mood episode, substance use, or medical/neurological cause supports schizophrenia, catatonic type. No new findings ruled this out.

doctor.intent: Screen for a concurrent major depressive episode (e.g., persistent sadness, hopelessness, guilt, or anhedonia) to rule out a mood disorder with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder
doctor.question: During these past six months, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or down on yourself, more days than not?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is asking about persistent depressed mood, hopelessness, or low self-worth, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think it’s been like that, no… not more days than not. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, especially when I mess things up or people are disappointed, but I wouldn’t say I’m just sad all the time or hopeless.

Maybe I’ve been more stressed than anything. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. If you mean like depressed every day, I don’t think that’s really me.

inference.note: Catatonic behaviors (posturing, echolalia/echopraxia, stereotyped patterning), disorganized speech, and functional decline over 6 months with no mood episode, no substance/medical cause, and no clear hallucinations/delusions support schizophrenia, catatonic type. No new disorders added or ruled out this turn.
